subject: Post-call recap: caching assumptions & pricing follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex@fastretail.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-05T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: caching assumptions & pricing follow-up

Alex - thanks for the time today. Quick recap and next steps from our end so we stay aligned: 

Call recap:
- Use case: customer-facing chat + semantic search for product catalog (mixed chat + embeddings).
- Estimated volume (from you): rough ballpark discussed is hundreds of millions of tokens/month (we'll confirm exact split).
- Primary ask: understand how caching changes effective $/1M tokens and what hit rates we should model for pricing.

Key open items for pricing qualification:
1) Monthly token volume (average) and peak QPS/requests - helps with Dedicated sizing vs hosted.
2) Typical prompt reuse patterns (system prompts, templates, instruction prefixes) - these are the main source of cache hits.
3) Whether you can share a small anonymized sample of traffic (timestamps + prompt fingerprints) so our infra team can estimate practical prefix hit rates.

What we'll send by EOD:
- A short pricing scenarios sheet with 3 hit-rate cases (conservative/base/aggressive) and resulting effective $/1M tokens.
- Notes on our prefix-caching assumptions and examples of what gets cached (system/assistant prefixes, repeated user prompts).

Target next steps:
- You share sample logs (anonymized) or a small export -> we run a quick analysis (1-2 business days).
- 30-min follow-up with Marcus (solutions) and Aditya (inference) to validate hit rates and sizing.

Thanks -
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
(555) 555-1212

Attachment: 20260305-redwood-pricing-scenarios.xlsx (pricing scenarios & unit economics)

From: Alex Johnson <alex@fastretail.com>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-05T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: caching assumptions & pricing follow-up

Marissa - thanks for the summary. A couple quick clarifications so your scenarios are accurate:

- Our current estimate is ~250M tokens/month (mix of chat+embeddings). Peak traffic is around 5k requests/sec for searches during promotions.
- Budget range (initial pilot): $10k-$15k/month; if the economics look good we could expand.
- Prompt reuse: we have a lot of standardized system prompts and product-description templates. My guess is prefix reuse is significant - maybe 20-40% of requests share long identical prefixes (but I can only confirm with logs).

I'll upload an anonymized sample of request headers and prompt fingerprints to the Drive link tonight. Please mark anything sensitive.

- Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of AI Product, FastRetail
alex@fastretail.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex@fastretail.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-06T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: caching assumptions & pricing follow-up

Alex - appreciate the quick reply. Attached is the pricing scenarios workbook (20260305-redwood-pricing-scenarios.xlsx) and a short PDF describing the caching assumptions (sample-cache-assumptions.pdf). Key excerpts pasted below so you have the headline numbers immediately: 

Caching hit-rate scenarios (prefix/persistent cache):
- Conservative: 5% hit rate (low reuse) -> Effective tokens billed = 95% of raw tokens -> Effective price = $2.85 / 1M tokens
- Base: 20% hit rate (typical template reuse) -> Effective tokens billed = 80% of raw tokens -> Effective price = $2.40 / 1M tokens
- Aggressive: 45% hit rate (highly templated prompts + prefix caching) -> Effective tokens billed = 55% of raw tokens -> Effective price = $1.65 / 1M tokens

Assumptions behind the numbers:
- Baseline raw unit price used: $3.00 per 1M tokens for the model configuration we discussed (mixed chat + embed workload). This is the hosted list unit for the baseline model; reserved capacity pricing/commit can be lower - we can model that if you commit.
- Effective price = raw_price * (1 - hit_rate). Example: base case $3.00 * (1 - 0.20) = $2.40 / 1M effective tokens.
- Prefix caching: we assume caching of system prompts, instruction templates, and repeated user-prefixes up to N tokens (e.g., first 256 tokens). Cache hits avoid full model forward for prefix tokens; billing rules vary slightly by model, but we model the conservative case where only non-replayed tokens are billed.
- For embeddings: we model embedding queries separately (no token-level caching) - if a majority of your embeddings are dedupable we can show further savings.

Example unit-econ table (from workbook):
- Raw monthly tokens: 250,000,000
- Base case billed tokens after 20% hit: 200,000,000 -> billed units (per 1M) = 200 -> cost = 200 * $2.40 = $480
  (note: this is illustrative; see workbook for full math including request/response split)

Next steps I recommend immediately:
1) You upload 24-72h of anonymized prompt hashes + timestamps (we only need prompt fingerprints and length bins).
2) Marcus/Aditya will run a quick analysis and return a 1-page hit-rate distribution and sizing recommendation for Dedicated vs hosted.
3) Schedule 30-min follow-up - I put a tentative slot on the calendar (link below).

Thanks -
Marissa
Attachment: sample-cache-assumptions.pdf

From: Alex Johnson <alex@fastretail.com>

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

- Alex
